answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by funneling identity verification through a staking inlet, where minting each node requires cryptographic stake burning. To anchor hardware scarcity, nodes bind physical root keys to copper circuits and walnut casing chips. The burnt deposit scales superlinearly as $C(n) = k \cdot n^{1.5}$, imposing superlinear costs that render mass clone generation economically unviable.
